key_insight: quspect selects routing candidates by their cost after coupling-constrained resynthesis, reducing two-qubit gate counts compared with established compiler baselines.
engineering_relevance: Jointly considering routing and resynthesis can produce shallower, lower-entangling-gate circuits for connectivity-constrained quantum hardware.
method: Screen routing candidates and compare their post-resynthesis costs.
Use parity-state A* for small CNOT-phase regions and heuristic synthesis for larger regions.
Apply numerical three-qubit instantiation with a per-block 10^-9 check.
evidence_signal: Across 55 circuits from 41 papers on five topologies, quspect used 0.616× Qiskit O3's two-qubit gates (95% circuit-cluster bootstrap interval: 0.555–0.679) and 0.592× its depth; it also achieved the fewest CZ gates in all six main-run hardware scenarios.
watch_item: A* certifies minimum CX count only for a fixed phase polynomial when it reaches a goal within budget, not global optimality of the full compilation.
paper_title: Circuit compilation in the quspect quantum SDK: selecting routings after coupling-constrained resynthesis
